title: Power outage, disaster, or recovery
description: Puerto Rico had documented island-wide blackouts in this period: a power-plant fire in September 2016, Hurricanes Irma and Maria in September 2017 (full restoration took about 11 months), earthquakes in January 2020, and Hurricane Fiona in September 2022. A dip followed by a rise can mean disruption and recovery, not growth.
investigate: Do these events appear in the annual values at all — or does a yearly average smooth them away? Who lived through the slowest restorations, and where?
evidenceNote: The sources below document that these outages happened. Whether and how they appear in this case study's annual values has not yet been tested.

title: Rebuilding, electrification or construction
description: Repairs and rebuilding after the hurricanes, new grid equipment, or new buildings and roads could add or restore light.
investigate: Where was the grid rebuilt, and was it rebuilt to the same pattern? Who decided where light came back first?

title: Lighting technology or public-lighting policy changed
description: Replacing street lights — for example with LEDs — or changing lighting hours can change recorded brightness, up or down, without any change in activity.
investigate: Were public lights replaced or repaired differently after the storms?

title: Changes in who lives here and how places are used
description: People moving away or returning, homes left empty, or changes in work and tourism could all change how much light a place gives off.
investigate: Did the number of occupied homes or the pattern of night-time activity change over the period?

title: Generators, vehicles, ports, or other non-home light sources
description: Power plants, ports, highways, industrial sites and large backup generators can all be recorded as night-time light.
investigate: What lies inside the grid cells that changed most — homes, a road, a port, a plant?

title: Cloud cover or processing differences
description: Years with few cloud-free nights, or differences in how the provider screened and combined observations, can shift values on their own.
investigate: How many cloud-free observations support each year, and did the product version or method change?
